get.description:
The portfolio at a glance, in one call: every account with its unit resources (each with the version, state digest, record count and time of its last import, and that import's verification summary `{status, verified_at, failed}` in policy 03 contract rule 2.6.1's shape), its open items counted by kind, its resources counted by verification status (`none`: without one), and its newest sync job; then the same counts for the whole portfolio, and its newest sync job.

No unit is called: each verification is the one the resource's last import copied, which describes the imported version or an earlier one. A resource's live state is its unit's `GET /resources/{r}`. Open items are those of `GET {P}/items`; an item concerning several accounts counts once in each, and once in the portfolio's counts. `pnl` is the portfolio's P&L now (its live MTM P&L, with NAV and net contributions) and its breakdown from the live books (policy 05 rule 43): realized P&L, income and expenses by label, unrealized P&L (live value − remaining cost, valued now) and `not_in_books` with its named `causes`, adding up to P&L; with its basis and `updating`; null before the live books are computed (a live job is queued).

get.description:
The portfolio's value in the reporting currency, in one call: the total and every active account's, each split into `assets` (valued holdings), `debt` (valued liabilities, zero or negative) and `value` (net assets = assets + debt), with counts of valued holdings, gaps and holdings not valued by design, `mostly_unvalued`, and each account's `share` of the net total; then the portfolio's price gaps counted by reason, and `complete`.

A gap (`no_price`, `stale_price`, `no_mark`, `fx`, `unresolved_asset`, `unbooked_liability`) is never counted as zero: it leaves its totals incomplete. `nft` and `lp_position` holdings are unvalued by design and keep a total complete; spam, possible spam and unassessable compartments are `excluded`. The numbers are those of `GET {P}/state?valued=true`, whose rows carry each holding's value and `share`.

post.description: Queue a correction job that applies the correction, recorded with the token's subject, the time and the job, or previews it (`?dry_run=true`, which needs only `read`); poll `GET /jobs/{id}`, whose `result` is the `CorrectionResult`. `merge_internal` links a withdrawal and a deposit as one internal movement; `classify_boundary` tags an unlinked transfer as a boundary transfer with the counterparty on the other side (policy 05 sub-ledger Rule 3.3): an id from `GET {P}/counterparties`, or `{label, mine, note?, reference?}`, created in the same job; `replaces` withdraws that tag of the same record in the same job. Its counterparty's flag decides the booking (Rule 2): someone else, at market value both ways; mine, out at cost and in at market value as the new cost; never income or expense. `ownership_retained` is derived from the flag, and one that disagrees is a 422. The correction records the token's subject, the job and, for an agent's API key, the AI-made mark. The result's `effect` lists the records concerned (before/after: `link`, `classified`, `unmatched`), the links added, the open items resolved, added or changed, and the balances that move. The records are checked before the job is queued, and again by the job: they must be unlinked, unclassified transfers (404 `record-not-found` or `counterparty-not-found`, 409 `correction-conflict`, 422 otherwise). An identical request of the same user joins the job already queued or running.

post.description: Seal the books at `as_of` (default: the end of the latest import) for a `reason` (policy 05 rule 37.2): `export`, `final` (needs `admin`; the revision is then marked final, rule 37.3) or `snapshot`. Nothing seals automatically. When a revision under the current policy with the same `as_of` and input digest exists, it is reused: answered at once (200, `reused`) when the live books at that `as_of` are cached and current, else found by the seal job once it has translated and priced, before it runs anything else. Otherwise the job translates the ledger up to `as_of`, fetches the daily prices its events need (never prices of holdings, rule 1.5), validates, runs the engine, audits, and seals the package (records, links, policy, coverage, corrections, the prices the events used, engine input and output with its rows and open-lot rows, audit, and every cited evidence object fetched from its unit; no series and no valuation, rule 23.5) as a new immutable revision recording its reason and input digest; its progress names each step, packaging and storing included. The result is the books summary with its `revision_id`, `reason` and `reused`. A person's run holds one job token for reading evidence from the units, revoked when it ends; a run started with an API key reads with that key (403 `key-audience-missing` when its audience lacks a unit). A seal at the same `as_of` already queued or running is returned instead. Needs `correct` (`admin` for `final`).

post.description: Queue a replay of a sealed revision: verify every file of its package against the manifest and the records' evidence closure, check the pinned engine is the installed one, rebuild the engine input from the pinned records, links and policy, run the engine again, and check its rows files. No unit or provider is called and nothing changes. The result says whether the books `matched` and how many files were verified. A replay of the same revision already queued or running is returned instead. Needs `read` (policy 05 rule 36: a check that changes nothing).

post.description: Mark a revision final for its `as_of` (policy 05 rule 26): the books the portfolio stands behind for that date, replacing the revision that was final for it (both stay). Open issues (`GET {P}/books/{rev}`'s `issues`: price gaps, engine exceptions, unbooked records, series points not valued, `failed` and `unassessable` coverage) never forbid it and need no acknowledgement; any given are recorded with their reason and count, and one that names no open issue is a 422. The mark records who made it and when, and states the revision's open-issue count (`open_issues`). A revision sealed without an `as_of` cannot be final (422). Needs `admin`.

delete.description: Unmark a final revision: its `as_of` has no final books until another is marked. 404 when it is not final. Needs `admin`.

get.description: The live layer's headline figures (policy 05 rules 36 and 39.1), without books: at every UTC day end (or the last of each month) from `from` to `to`, live NAV (holdings and opaque compartments valued, net of liabilities, plus open positions' unrealized P&L at the mark), net contributions (boundary transfers at their market value) and MTM P&L = NAV − contributions, each point `complete` or listing the assets not valued (`missing`; never valued at zero). Joined with the live books by default (`revision=live`, rule 36; a sealed revision when named), each point they cover adds its realized results to date (`realized`: realized P&L + income − expenses) and `unrealized` = MTM P&L − realized (rule 39.12.1): the live books cover every point, since nothing after the latest import is known, and are valued at the time of reading (decision 33); a sealed revision covers the points up to its `as_of`, which is a point too. `revision` states the basis (rule 34): its id, `as_of`, policy, `valued_at`, and for the live books `updating` (a live job is computing them again) or `computed: false` (not computed yet: no point carries realized results, and a live job is queued). `warning` states why the books' total P&L at `as_of` (realized + per-holding unrealized) differs from the live MTM P&L, by cause (rule 39.5.2); it is never folded into unrealized P&L. Values are computed when read and may change with prices or valuation rules (`computed_at`). 404 for an unknown revision (or none under the current policy for `current`); 409 `rows-unavailable` for one sealed without rows.

get.description: P&L by asset, account, month or year (policy 05 rules 36, 43.2 and 44.5), from the live books by default (or a sealed revision), with the portfolio's `total`: P&L now and its breakdown, whose lines add up to it. Each group carries realized P&L, income and expenses (with `flows` by label), unrealized P&L, `not_in_books` and P&L. An asset group adds the remaining `cost` of its holdings, valued now for the live books (decision 33). An account group's P&L is its live MTM P&L (`nav` − `contributions`), its booked figures components and the rest unrealized, `pooled` under the `global` lot scope (decision 34). A month or year group is dated in the portfolio's `time_zone`; its P&L is the MTM P&L at its end less at its start, its booked figures those of the period and its unrealized P&L the change over it. `from` and `to` narrow the booked figures to those days. `basis` states the books and when holdings are valued (rule 34). 409 `live-books-missing` before the live books are computed (a live job is queued). Needs `read`.

post.description:
Queue a sync of the given accounts, else of every active one (archived accounts never sync): per resource a unit sync (a child job), then the import, then a reconcile of the whole portfolio (policy 01 portfolio Rule 10; its summary, or its error, is the result's `reconcile`); a sync already queued or running for the portfolio is returned instead. The job's `accounts` are fixed now (every active account, for a sync of all).

An account still mapped by its resource's id from before its unit (dydx, evm, hl) assigned UUIDs is resolved by name first, with the request's credential, and its UUID recorded (policy 03 contract gap 26). A budget is a hard limit (policy 02 access Rule 7.2): a resource its unit refuses over its budget is listed under the result's `over_budget`, and nothing passes it.

A person's sync holds one job token for the units and resources it calls, requested now from their session (403 `grant-refused` when platform refuses it, 502 `grant-failed` when it cannot answer) and revoked when the job ends or is cancelled. A sync started with an API key calls the units with that key: 403 `key-audience-missing` when its audience lacks one of them.

post.description:
Queue a rebuild of the whole ledger, a sync job of every active account (`request.rebuild`) that replaces the ledger instead of each account's records: the upgrade step after the units' records move to a new schema generation, which an account-by-account import refuses to mix.

Every account's current unit state is imported from `changes?since=0` (unit syncs first only with `refresh: true`), and in one transaction the records, machine and adapter links, coverage and stored holdings and open items are deleted, the imports rewritten, every account's records and coverage derived again and the ledger reconciled. Accounts, unit resources, settings, policy, corrections (with the links they own), prices and the import history stay; a merge whose record did not come back is pruned and becomes a `failed_correction` item. Any failure, or any account that cannot be imported, fails the job and leaves the previous ledger untouched. Needs `admin` (policy 02 access Rule 7: it deletes derived data); a sync already queued or running for the portfolio is returned instead.
